subject: physics
title: Forces & Motion - Application
welcome_lead: Time to put forces to work in real-world situations.
meta_desc: KS3 Physics: apply force concepts to balanced/unbalanced forces and everyday motion.
final_note: You can now predict how forces will affect motion. Nice work!

concepts.def: Equal forces in opposite directions - no change.
Unequal forces - cause speed or direction change.
Single force equal to all forces combined.
Friction from air slowing moving objects.
Unit of force; 1 N pushes 1 kg by 1 m/s every second.
Friction force from a fluid (air or water).

walkthroughs.body_html:
When forces on an object are equal and opposite, they cancel out.

A book on a table: gravity pulls down, table pushes up. Forces balance, book stays still.

Balanced forces mean: stationary objects stay still, or moving objects keep the same speed and direction.

If forces don't cancel, there's a resultant force. This makes things change.

Push a trolley with 20 N forward, friction pushes back with 5 N. Resultant = 15 N forward. The trolley speeds up.

Unbalanced forces cause objects to accelerate, slow down, or change direction.

Friction always opposes motion. It can be helpful or annoying.

Helpful: brakes on bikes, grip on shoes.

Unhelpful: slows machines, wastes energy as heat. We use oil to reduce it.

Air resistance is just friction with air - a parachute uses it to slow a skydiver.

mcqs.q: A car drives at a constant speed. What does this tell us about the forces?
Which would reduce friction between machine parts?

numericals.q: A box has a 30 N force pushing right and a 12 N friction force opposing. What is the resultant force?

free_texts.q: What word describes a single force that has the same effect as all the forces on an object combined?
free_texts.hint: It's the net or overall force.
